title: LCI: a Lightweight Communication Interface for Efficient Asynchronous Multithreaded Communication
problem: Evolving architectures, programming models, and algorithms demand greater asynchrony and concurrency in multithreaded environments, but existing communication libraries are not optimized for such patterns.
motivation: Modern HPC systems require efficient asynchronous multithreaded communication. Traditional communication libraries like MPI focus on multi-process models, which are suboptimal for shared-memory multithreaded scenarios.
method: LCI provides a threading-efficient communication library built on atomic data structures, fine-grained non-blocking locks, and low-level network insights. Features include concise point-to-point primitives, diverse completion mechanisms, and flexible resource control.
key_novelty: Threading-efficient runtime designed specifically for asynchronous multithreaded communication with low-overhead synchronization primitives and fine-grained resource controls.
contributions: Significant performance gains over existing communication libraries in multithreaded scenarios
Performance exceeding traditional multi-process execution mode
Support for diverse completion mechanisms (polling, callbacks, events)
Flexible controls for incrementally fine-tuning communication resources and runtime behavior
Open-source implementation with support for Infiniband and Slingshot-11
limitations: Full-text not available; specific performance numbers not disclosed in abstract. Detailed microbenchmark results not provided.
